content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I work with [article_no] [product_name]. I want to access some [product_name] inputs and outputs using LabVIEW via Modbus I/O server or an OPC server. So far, I haven't managed to get this working, which is why I'm posting here. Has anyone successfully connected [product_name] and LabVIEW using any tools? Thanks in advance!
Maybe this [url] can be useful: S7 PLC TCP/IP Protocol Reference Example.

Thank you [user_name]! I checked the article you provided from NI, but unfortunately it wasn't useful since it focused on S7 communication protocol, and I'm specifically trying to connect with Modbus TCP/IP. I've also tried the NI Modbus library, but ended up with the same issue.

[product_name] uses Ethernet TCP/IP with the S7 protocol. It utilizes VM memory for data exchange, which remote devices can read or write as a datablock (DB1). For example: Bit = V0.0 = DB1.DBX0.0; Byte = VB0 = DB1.DBB0; Word = VW0 = DB1.DBW0; DWord = VD0 = DB1.DBD0. Edit: [product_name] versions [version_no] or later also support Modbus TCP/IP, allowing you to use the VM memory and transfer data such as input/output holding registers.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is attempting to set up communication between a [product_name] controller and LabVIEW using Modbus or OPC, but encounters challenges achieving a working connection. The thread references a specific hardware model and asks for practical guidance or confirmation about integrating with LabVIEW. Responses clarify protocol compatibility and memory mapping, but underline confusion regarding protocol support in different [product_name] models and versions. There is a mismatch between the user's hope for straightforward LabVIEW integration via Modbus TCP/IP and the actual protocol implementations in various [product_name] devices.
